Published: 16:27 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:07 EST, 23 November 2026

Arsenal will be keeping everything crossed ahead of goalkeeper David Raya undergoing tests on what appeared to be a shoulder or arm injury sustained against Newcastle.

The Gunners' No1 went off in the second half in the 2-2 draw at St James' Park, supporting his arm or shoulder before he was replaced by back-up Kepa Arrizabalaga.

It leaves everyone associated with Arsenal nervous, as they face potentially a sustained period of time without a key part of their impressive defence.

Raya appeared to pick up the injury by running into Newcastle's Will Osula after claiming the ball from a cross.

As he attempted to run forward to start an attack, he collided with the striker and hit the ground in pain.

After a brief period of treatment on the field, he was substituted, supporting his arm, and replaced in the game.

"I'm petrified!" Ian Wright and Jamie Redknapp on why David Raya coming off injured vs Newcastle is a massive worry for Arsenal 🧤 pic.twitter.com/F5uAgjFdp0

Arsenal face a nervy wait to find out the extent of David Raya's injury picked up against Newcastle on Saturday

Manager Mikel Arteta has been left sweating at the idea of being without his No1 for a busy Christmas period.

'Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news,' Arteta said: 'He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don't know.

'It was a knock, I don't know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment. We have to wait and see tomorrow.

'We know how important David is for us. Tomorrow we will have more news.'

The Gunners will play nine more games before the end of the year as they look to push forward in both the league and Champions League.

That challenge has just got harder, though, and Arsenal fan and former forward Ian Wright has expressed his concern.

'That's a massive worry,' he said on Sky Sports. 'I don't want to say I'm petrified simply because Kepa is in goal, he's the guy who has got to try and keep the goals out for us now.

'But yeah, that is a massive blow. Someone like him, Declan Rice, Gabriel, it is very tough to replace those guys.'

David Moyes is unsure as to whether or not Everton will appeal the red card shown to James Tarkowski in the 4-0 defeat to Brentford on Monday night.

The centre-back received his marching orders in the 40th minute for a studs-up challenge on Yehor Yarmolyuk, with Craig Pawson upgrading his decision from a yellow card after viewing the pitchside VAR monitor.

The 34-year-old is set to face a three-match suspension, starting with the Merseyside derby next Sunday and also ruling out of the subsequent games against Aston Villa and Fulham.

When speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Moyes was asked whether Everton would appeal Tarkowski’s red card, to which he simply replied: “Don’t know yet.”

The Toffees manager later admitted that he’d revised his original stance on the incident, saying (via Liverpool Echo): “My first feeling at the time was I didn’t think it was red because I thought James easily got to the ball before Yehor Yarmolyuk.

“I could have said that the Brentford player was a bit late in getting there, but after seeing it again I can see that Tarky’s boot is a bit higher than I like, so I can understand why the decision went against us.”

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The rights or wrongs of the red card decision will be debated throughout the week, but Tarkowski didn’t do his Everton teammates any favours with his lunge on Yarmolyuk, especially when they were already 2-0 down and just about still in the contest at that point.

His suspension for the next three games (pending an appeal) also comes as a blow to the Toffees, particularly ahead of the derby next Sunday, when he won’t get the chance to replicate his stoppage-time equaliser from the memorable Goodison Park clash two seasons ago.

Moyes now has just two centre-backs available for the game against Liverpool in Jarrad Branthwaite and Michael Keane, so the Scot will be living on his nerves this week that neither of those succumb to injury in the coming days.

That the Everton boss felt the red card was justified seems telling, and Tarkowski will be bitterly disappointed with his rush of blood to the head last night.

The Toffees’ task of recording a first derby win since April 2024 has become notably harder without the experienced defender, unless they lodge (and win) an appeal, which right now seems improbable.

#1227. Three Italians ruled out for several months with serious injuries after Serie A Week 12

Three Italian players are set for lengthy spells on the sidelines after the latest round of Serie A fixtures, including two members of Roberto Mancini’s most recent national team squad.

Napoli’s Antonio Vergara, Atalanta’s Marco Carnesecchi and Genoa’s Lorenzo Colombo are all expected to miss several months of action with serious injuries they suffered during the 12th round of 2026-27 Serie A fixtures.

Vergara was visibly distressed when he was forced out of Napoli’s 1-0 win over Torino, making way for Kevin De Bruyne after just 11 minutes.

Napoli confirmed in a statement on Monday that he has undergone medical tests that have revealed a high-grade tear to the biceps femoris muscle in his left thigh and according to reports from Sky Sport Italia, this will keep him out of action for a minimum of two months. Other outlets suggest that the timeline will be closer to three months.

Atalanta stopper Carnesecchi, meanwhile, is due to undergo surgery on his knee on Tuesday after suffering a tear of the medial meniscus in his left knee after pulling up injured in the warm-up of his side’s 4-4 draw against Inter on Sunday evening.

It remains unclear exactly how long the 26-year-old will miss, but initial reports suggest that he will be ruled out until January at least.

It was also confirmed on Monday that Genoa striker Colombo has suffered an injury to the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) of his right knee. Again, an exact recovery time has not been specified, but his injury is the most serious of the three and some reports suggest that his 2026-27 season could be over.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1225. Hull reignite genuine survival hopes with late Oli McBurnie double to down Brighton, as talk of Seagulls emulating Leicester City-style fairytale is made to look foolish

Published: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:08 EST, 23 November 2026

When Brighton owner Tony Bloom was asked about his club’s title prospects last week, he suggested they could emulate Leicester City’s 2015-16 fairytale and win the Premier League.

It was a bold claim, yet Fabian Hurzeler’s men looked anything but title aspirants after being downed by Oli McBurnie’s dramatic late double for newly-promoted Hull City.

Brighton have been the most credible challengers to Arsenal so far this season. That cannot be denied.

With Manchester City wobbling alarmingly, and the rest of the traditional big guns largely off the title pace, the Seagulls have at least given Mikel Arteta’s champions something to think about.

But this bitterly cold afternoon in East Yorkshire was a reality check for Hurzeler’s men and a harsh lesson in taking the chances that come your way.

Brighton didn’t and McBurnie most certainly did, firing home clinically from close range twice in added time shortly after Joao Costinha had been sent off.

Oli McBurnie scored a late brace to secure a brilliant three points for Hull against Brighton

McBurnie has made a habit of leaving it late – the rejuvenated Scotland striker struck a 95th-minute winner in the Championship play-off final against Middlesbrough at Wembley in May.

Hull had gone eight Premier League games without a win before Brighton’s visit and this success lifted them to 11th.

Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic said of McBurnie: 'I’ve never had any doubts over a ‘Braveheart’ like Oli because he’s a natural leader and very important for us.'

Asked where the setback left Brighton’s title hopes, Hurzeler said: 'We don’t focus on the table – we focus on performances and how we can make the right improvements into the team.

'That’s the same if we had won or lost, but today showed there are still things we need to do better. That’s what we will do and then see what the outcome will be.'

Brighton arrived as favourites and could have cut Arsenal's lead at the top of the table

Hull were indebted to a remarkable display from their Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who reduced Brighton to an afternoon of frustration and futility.

The visitors had 10 attempts at goal during the first half alone, forcing Hull’s summer signing into a string of fine saves and also being denied by the woodwork.

At times the Seagulls’ pretty patterns threatened to cut the Tigers apart as the likes of Maxim De Cuyper, Diego Gomez and the effervescent Pascal Gross – on his 300th appearance for the club – knitted them together superbly.

Georginio Rutter was involved in a move which saw De Cuyper cross low from the left flank to the onrushing Gomez, whose close-range effort was superbly saved by Tzolakis.

That set the tone for an outstanding display by the 24-year-old Greece international, who arrived in the summer from Olympiacos as part of the newly-promoted Tigers’ £150million spending spree which saw 18 players signed.

Hull lacked nothing in spirit and fight but Brighton had the quality and constantly threatened to open up their hosts.

As half-time approached, Rutter saw a close-range shot repelled by Tzolakis after Yasin Ayari’s effort rebounded off the crossbar.

The Tigers were constantly grateful to their goalkeeper, who made another save to keep out an effort from Gomez on the stroke of half-time.

Tzolakis continued to prove unbeatable in the second half too, and his opposite number Bart Verbruggen was left grateful to the woodwork after a cross-shot from substitute Sorba Thomas hit the crossbar.

Mohamed Belloumi was also a lingering threat for Hull on the right flank and he should have scored after cutting infield before firing wastefully wide.

Konstantinos Tzolakis (right) produced a remarkable display to keep Brighton out

As the game wore on, there was an inescapable feeling that Brighton could be punished for their wastefulness as Hull showed the kind of courage which deserves, and usually gets, its rewards.

Regan Slater cleared a shot from Charalampos Kostoulas off the line before Brighton lost Joao Costinha to a second yellow card with a minute remaining.

The Tigers sensed blood, pouring forward to lead in the first minute of added time as McBurnie expertly sidefooted them in front from Lucas Gourna-Douath’s neat pass to cap a delightful flowing move.

Moments before the final whistle, Hull struck again as McBurnie swept home from close range again from Mo Belloumi’s assist. Cue delirium in the home stands.

McBurnie took the acclaim but Tzolakis was Hull’s star man as Jakirovic acknowledged: 'Tzolakis was amazing and we could have been two or three-nil down without his saves.

'We stayed alive because of him and then won the game at the end. Ciao!'

Hull had failed to win since beating Manchester United and Coventry in their opening two games in August.

Hull reignited their survival hopes with a precious win against an in-form team

Crucially, however, they have been competitive in every game this season and are now unbeaten in six home matches.

Can they survive? 'Of course, and every win is so important,' declared Jakirovic.

'I wish this feeling I have now would never stop but I know how demanding this league is.'

#1224. Milan strike €5m agreement with Eintracht Frankfurt for new Head of Football Krösche

Multiple outlets in Italy and Germany are reporting that Milan have reached an agreement with Eintracht Frankfurt over the compensation for Markus Krösche, who is set to join the Rossoneri in the role of Head of Football.

According to Sky Sport DE and various other sources, Milan have triggered a release clause and will pay Eintracht Frankfurt a fee in the region of €5m for Krösche’s services. Reports back in October indicate that there was already an agreement in principle between Milan and Krösche in place.

Krösche left his position with the Bundesliga club earlier this season, but Frankfurt are reportedly owed compensation if he takes on another job before the summer of 2027.

Monday’s reports claim that Krösche will take over in the role of Head of Football at Milan on January 1, 2027.

Milan have been looking to appoint Krösche since the summer. The club has restructured its senior management team after parting company with head coach Massimiliano Allegri, sporting director Igli Tare, technical director Geoffrey Moncada and CEO Giorgio Furlani in one fell swoop the day after the 2025-26 season ended.

Since then, Massimo Calvelli has served as CEO, Hendrik Almstadt has been serving as director of player trading and Bobby Gardiner is the director of football intelligence.

Krösche is now set to joining them, overseeing in the role of Head of Football.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1223. Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

Having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area showed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

But after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm

And that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”

The Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

“It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

“It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

“We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

“They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

“It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”

Leeds are the kind of compact, organised, aggressive in-your-face team United have tended to struggle against in recent years. They were good in defeat to Arsenal last weekend and showcased their considerable threat in the 4-1 win over Newcastle. Expect a white-hot atmosphere at Elland Road. They cannot stand Manchester United in these parts.

Lisandro Martínez delivered a strong and powerful message to his Manchester United team-mates: if you’re playing terribly, use the director of football as a punchbag and you might become a hero.

It is a popular play in a world in which certain players have become as adept at scapegoat-hunting as man-marking. Passionately speak about what someone else at your football club is doing wrong – particularly the unloved executives – and cast yourself as a whistleblower, selflessly exposing the truth that the long-suffering supporters deserve.

Such internal fights make for great drama, unless your own club is caught in the middle of it.

That’s why in the immediate aftermath of Martínez’s scathing comments about Jason Wilcox following the Champions League defeat by Atlético Madrid, there was a division between those who celebrated the Argentine speaking out and those who felt it was self-serving, a convenient deflection by an out-of-form player in the final year of his contract.

The narrative is completely dominated by the drama around Man Utd, which should suit Leeds perfectly. All eyes and pressure is on their opponents, and they have every reason to feel confident ahead of this huge clash at Elland Road.

#1222. Stat Proving Man Utd’s Likelihood of Getting Relegated Goes Viral

It seems wild to even consider, but Manchester United are in a relegation fight right now. After 11 Premier League games, the Red Devils sit one point and one place above the bottom of the table.

Michael Carrick managed to win just one game, picking up eight points from a possible 30 before he was sacked. Mauricio Pochettino has replaced the Englishman, but any hopes of an immediate new-manager bouncequickly evaporated at Anfield over the weekend.

Man Utd were trounced 4-0 by their bitter rivals. After the game, Pochettino conceded his team were in a relegation battle, stating: "Relegation battle? That is our reality, no…? We are there. We need to win games."

Omar Berrada's old Man Utd tweets have gone viral after the team were thrashed 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.

There are all sorts of stats to tell you just how badly things are going for the Red Devils. As per TNT Sports, for instance, across Europe's top five leagues this season, no side has conceded more goals than Man United (34).

Moreover, Pochettino's 4-0 debut loss to Liverpool was the joint-worst result for any new United boss, matching the 4-0 loss Lal Hilditch suffered against Bolton in October 1926. The English coach lasted 30 games and never managed another team.

But there is one stat that really captures the doom and gloom at Old Trafford right now. Indeed, a post from ESPN writer Mark Ogden has gone viral as it outlines just how likely Man Utd are to be relegated from the Premier League this term. He wrote:

"Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and stayed up on the final day. United have 8 points from 11 games."

Spurs avoided the drop by two points, with West Ham going down instead. Last term also saw Burnley and Wolves relegated with ease. Things could be a lot tighter in 2026/27, though, with no obvious candidate to go down as things stand.

The post has almost two million views on X and has generated thousands of likes and hundreds of comments. One noted: "Penny beginning to drop, United are in serious trouble."

Another said: "Most people haven’t clocked it yet but we are actually getting relegated."

And a third added: "This is when it really hits home." Someone else summed up the mood, noting: "This is bleak for United."

If Man Utd do go down, it won't be uncharted territory for the club. While they've not been relegated in the Premier League era, they have suffered that misery on five occasions across their history.

The first came in 1893/94, when they were still known as Newton Heath, and finished bottom of the First Division. Relegations then followed in 1921/22, 1930/31 and 1936/37.

The most famous and most recent relegation came just six years after they became the first English club to win the European Cup. In the final round of fixturesfor the 1973/74 season, club legend Denis Law scored for rivals Man City as his former team were beaten 1-0 in the Manchester Derby.

Law barely reacted, but later described himself as "inconsolable" as Man Utd were relegated. Perhaps it came as some small consolation that Law's goal didn't end up sending the Red Devils down. Birmingham City's win over Norwich City and West Ham's draw with Liverpool meant United were relegated regardless.

Neutrals will be hoping for something just as dramatic in 2026/27.

#1219. Who is Markus Krösche and who are his best signings?

Monday’s reports claim that Milan have reached an agreement with Eintracht Frankfurt over the compensation for Markus Krösche, who is set to take over in the role of Head of Football at San Siro, but who is the 45-year-old executive and who are his most notable signings to date?

Krösche is a former holding midfielder who came through the youth and reserve ranks at Werder Bremen before joining SC Padderborn in 2001, where he would go on to spend the rest of his playing career. His 356 league outings for the German outfit makes him the club’s all-time record appearance holder.

Upon his retirement in 2014, Krösche has a brief stint in charge of SC Padderborn II, the club’s reserve side before going on to serve as an assistant coach to Roger Schmidt at Bayer Leverkusen between 2015 and 2017.

Krösche left Leverkusen when Schmidt was sacked towards the end of the 2016-17 season and decided to return to Padderborn in the role of managing director.

While in charge of Padderborn, Krösche oversaw back-to-back promotions from the third tier of German football to the top flight, which was only the second time in the club’s history that the club had featured in the Bundesliga.

This success earned Krösche a move to RB Leipzig to take over as sporting director, where he would serve for two seasons between 2019 and 2021.

In 2021, he joined Eintracht Frankfurt as sporting director, and until his resignation earlier this season, he had a member of the club’s board under the title ‘board member for sport’.

Krösche has overseen the transfers of a number of high-profile players across his time with Leipzig and Frankfurt, including the likes of Dani Olmo, Josko Gvardiol, Randal Kolo Muani and Hugo Ekitike.

Below is a list of his most notable and most profitable signings to date.

Ademola Lookman: Everton → RB Leipzig (€18m)

Christopher Nkunku: PSG → RB Leipzig (€19.5m, later sold to Chelsea for €60m)

Dani Olmo: Dinamo Zagreb → RB Leipzig (€34m, later sold to Barcelona for €61m)

Josko Gvardiol: Dinamo Zagreb → RB Leipzig (€36m, later sold to Manchester City for €90m)

Lazar Samardzic: Hertha BSC → RB Leipzig (€500,000)

Josep Martinez: Las Palmas → RB Leipzig (€2.5m)

Randal Kolo Muani: FC Nantes → Eintracht Frankfurt (free, later sold to PSG for €95m)

Mario Götze: PSV → Eintracht Frankfurt (€4.5m)

Omar Marmoush: Wolfsburg → Eintracht Frankfurt (free, later sold to Manchester City for €75m)

Willian Pacho: Royal Antwerp → Eintracht Frankfurt (€13.5m, later sold to PSG for €40m)

Nathaniel Brown: 1.FC Nuremberg → Eintracht Frankfurt (€5.5m)

Hugo Ekitike: PSG → Eintracht Frankfurt (€31.5m, later sold to Liverpool for €95m)

#1218. Leny Yoro Is Quickly Becoming The Next Anthony Martial at Man Utd

Mauricio Pochettino learnt a lot about his Manchester United players in the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool on Sunday.

It was not the start that the Argentine was hoping for after replacing Michael Carrick in the dugout, but he did get to see how his players react to adversity, after an eighth minute red card for Leny Yoro turned the tide against them so early in the game.

It wasn't brilliant, and five minutes later they were 2-0 down after goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz, which ultimately put the game out of sight, even at that early stage.

United did avoid a total humiliation, but there are big question marks over the club's defenders, as they became the club to concede the most goals across Europe's top five leagues.

Matthijs de Ligt made a disastrous first Premier League start in almost a year, and it was his error that led to Yoro being red-carded so early on, after he failed to challenge for the ball.

Lisandro Martinez didn't look much better alongside him, while Diogo Dalot continues to look uncomfortable in the left-back position.

You had to feel sorry for Yoro though, who endured another disappointing evening in a Manchester United shirt as his Old Trafford career continus to stutter.

The 21-year-old, who joined United for a fee that could rise to £60m from Lille in 2024, was given his marching orders in the eighth minute for denying a goalscoring opportunity. A long ball over the top of the United back-line caused havoc, and after De Ligt misread the flight of the ball, Alexander Isak ran through on goal, only for Yoro to bring him down outside the box.

As Isak was about to shoot and have a chance at scoring, Yoro hauled him to the floor, and referee Sam Barrott had no choice but to brandish the red card.

It was the second time Yoro has been sent off this season, after he was given a red card during United's 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

He was at fault for Aston Villa's fourth goal in the 4-4 draw before the November international break, and has been part of a United defence that is the worst in Europe this season. Indeed, the Reds have conceded 34 goals across all competitions, the most out of Europe's top five leagues.

Yoro arrived at United with such huge hopes, having been named as the Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year in the previous season after impressing for Lille, but it just hasn't worked out for him at Old Trafford so far. Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick were all unable to get the best out of him, and now it's Mauricio Pochettino's turn to see if he can get him into form.

Judging off his eight-minute performance against Liverpool, Pochettino could have his work cut out. While Yoro would be available for Wednesday's trip to Sporting CP, he will be banned for United's next three Premier League matches against Brentford, Newcastle and Coventry.

If Pochettino can't get Yoro back to his best, there are fears his United career could dwindle as it did for fellow Frenchman Anthony Martial.

The ex-Monaco man, now 30, was touted as one of the most talented young players in world football before his £36m move to the Reds in 2015, when he was 19 years of age.

While he did impress at times, he flattered to deceive for the majority of his time in Manchester, especially in the latter years, and left in 2024.

Yoro will be desperate that doesn't happen, however, and he can have a long-lasting impact at United. At just 21, he has the age on his side and still has a lot of potential to develop.

Right now, it doesn't look great for him. United looked more solid in a back-five when Harry Maguire came on, and that is how Pochettino could line up going into the trip to Sporting. It would leave Yoro's hopes of starting put in serious doubt, though he has impressed in that shape before.

When he is given his next chance - which he will do at some point - Yoro has to take it. He has to be much better and show why United paid more than £50m to sign him. If he doesn't, he is in serious danger of becoming the next big money signing, like Martial, to flop.

Declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO

Delap with a tame shot from distance, before Timber instigates a more dangerous Arsenal attack with a reverse pass into Odegaard. The ball is worked to Madueke and his deflected cross is headed away. Saka wants a throw but the linesman has other ideas. Still no goal despite more endeavour in this half.

Arsenal building some pressure, and they have another corner. Arteta signalling that he wants to make the change before the corner is taken and here come the changes: White for Timber, Havertz for Gyokeres and Merino on for Bruno Guimaraes.

Gabriel meets Rice’s delivery, but he fails to direct his header on target.

Excellent defending from Gabriel up against Ndoye in the right channel, but it was another promising moment for Forest in this second half. Madueke then isolates his man one-on-one, and wins another corner.

Timber, Merino and Gyokeres are all ready to come on for Arsenal.

The game is see-sawing, Arsenal have a corner after Calafiori fed Madueke down the left and his cross was blocked. Sels punches away, and then Odegaard loses some patience and tries to find Calafiori with a pass that is not on.

Saka and Rice lose duels when fishing for fouls and Forest have another corner. Arsenal’s performance level has certainly not improved since half-time.

Arsenal clear, but Odegaard blocks a cross and Forest win a second corner in quick succession. Excellent goalkeeping from Raya to claim, and he bowls the ball forward quickly, but Forest snuff out the danger against Madueke.

The first half was an attack against defence session for long periods but Arsenal know they are in an arm wrestle now. Forest far more aggressive, and the crowd are more involved. But that could open up avenues of space. White with a really poor pass towards Saka which is astray.

Arsenal have a corner of their own after breaking from Raya’s gloves. Much more open game so far.

Forest deal with Saka’s delivery, and there was a very brief VAR check for a handball penalty. Nothing doing.

Madueke looking dangerous, receiving a Gabriel ball over the top and dashing inside but his shot was blocked.

The winger then tried to make amends, but he gave away a free-kick at the expense of a booking.

Delap’s shot from a tight angle is then deflected wide. Forest corner, from which Murillo’s header loops into Raya’s gloves. Forest showing more attacking ambition.

Liam Delap is producing a very decent centre-forward performance.

The £50m record signing is proving a real threat with his power and running.

Madueke and Rice not one the same wavelength, before Delap does well to win a shoulder to shoulder with Gabriel only to slice his cross behind for an Arsenal goal kick. Sums up the lack of attacking quality in the game.

Forest have another free-kick in a shooting position after Havertz is penalised for blocking a long shot with his hand. McAtee’s effort from the free-kick is scooped miles over the bar.

Both teams looking livelier in the early exchanges of the half, but Forest’s counter-attack was the more dangerous, with Liam Delap doing well to hold on to the ball and whipping a cross into the box that was just ahead of Williams.

Noni Madueke replaces Eberechi Eze, so a more natural wide player on his stronger foot on Arsenal’s left flank.

Frustrating first half for Arsenal and Mikel Arteta will be demanding more from his attacking players.

Arsenal have not registered a shot on target so far and their delivery from set-pieces has been poor.

Forest look relatively comfortable and had the best chance of the half with a shot from Dan Ndoye which was saved by David Raya.

Are we heading for a hat-trick of 0-0 draws at the City Ground between these two teams?

A very uneventful 45 minutes which has been played at the pace of a pre-season game at times. Similarities with the last two fixtures between these teams at the City Ground, and Arsenal’s games against Leeds and Lille this week. They put their foot on the pedal after half-time in both games, and they need to do the same here.

Guimaraes is off the pitch, and there will be more than two minutes added now as a result of his treatment. Forest win a corner, but Havertz heads away at the near post.

Just the two minutes of added time to play.

Liam Delap wins a free-kick in a shooting position for Forest after Arsenal were caught with numbers forward. Big moment for the home team, this. Calafiori was caught on the ball again, he has not had the best of games.

Williams and McAtee are over the free keek, which is around 25 yards out, left of centre.

Williams blasts the ball into Bruno Guimaraes, who goes down and stays down after taking the shot flush in the face.

More incisive from Arsenal, with Rice punching the ball into Odegaard and then on to Havertz but the angle was always against him and the German could only shoot into the side-netting. Forest have defended very well, overall. Although they have been deep for the most part, they have jumped and pushed out at the right times to stop Arsenal accessing the box.

Glasner and Arteta dish out some instruction while there is a stoppage in play to deal with a hand in the face that troubled Schlager. Can either side find a breakthrough before the break?

David Raya claimed that Forest corner with ease and the game has now resumed its pattern. Forest retreating into their shape, and Arsenal passing in front of them. Schlager penalised for a foul on Saka, the home fans not happy with the decision, I think because Saka was going away from goal.

Rice clips in a menacing delivery, but Havertz skewed his header wide from seven or eight yards. Good chance, Arsenal’s best so far.

More Arsenal probing but the small details are letting them down: Eze’s return to Odegaard forced his team-mate to check, and then Odegaard’s touch was heavy after a wall pass from Guimaraes.

Delap does well to make a nuisance of himself at the other end, and his long-range shot deflects behind for a corner.

Strong from Konsa to win the ball, drive out of defence and win a foul. Rice with a well-weighted scoop over the Forest defence for the run of Ben White, but he skewed his cross behind for a goal kick.

Arsenal with another corner. No doubt they have been the game’s dominant force when it comes to possession and territory, but there has been a lack of cutting edge so far. Saka goes for the near post again but Forest deal with it. The home crowd groan at Sels for not releasing the ball quickly in search of a break.

Arsenal work the ball across their midfield with Guimaraes, Rice and Odegaard all involved, and a dangerous Saka cross is headed behind for a corner.

Scramble! The near-post flick on caused chaos and Konsa’s goal-bound backheel was blocked, but the ball would not quite drop for Ben White to score a tap-in.

After two successive goalless draws here between the two clubs, this is following a similar script so far.

It’s a very tight affair with Arsenal enjoying more of the possession but Forest seemingly happy with that and content to them on the break.

Bruno Guimaraes has made a bright start for the visitors.

Forest’s best attacking moment of the game and it comes from an Arsenal mistake.

Calafiori just had to play a five-yard pass back to Gabriel but scuffed it, and Munoz pounced. Running at the Arsenal penalty area, Munoz’s cross was deflected to the back post and the ball found it’s way to Ndoye. Decent reverse shot through legs, but Raya had it covered and tipped around the post.

From the corner, Forest are penalised for a foul.

Arsenal continue to have Forest penned in their own half, very difficult for the home team to play through the midfield or over Konsa and Gabriel so far.

Saka produces his first successful dribble to beat Williams, and the left wing-back trips him at the expense of a free-kick and a booking. Rice’s delivery from the right was uncharacteristically poor.

Munoz tries to drag Forest up the pitch to apply some pressure on Arsenal but he is penalised for a shirt pull on Gabriel. The atmosphere sounds pretty sleepy, a result of some tepid Arsenal possession and Forest’s bad home record.

Forest making sure they have numbers around Saka whenever Arsenal funnel attacks down their right, which is almost always their preferred side.

Neat from Guimaraes in midfield to turn and find Saka with some earlier service, and Sels tips his cross away from danger.

Delap and Ndoye waiting for a slip-up or counter-attack but they are feeding on scraps at the moment. Arsenal yet to carve out a proper chance, though.

It’s already pretty clear that one of the key duels today will be between Gabriel and Liam Delap.

Forest’s record signing Delap has already let Gabriel know he’s in the game with his physicality.

Cute pass from Bruno Guimaraes to break the Forest midfield line and find Odegaard, but strangely the Arsenal captain could not sort his feet out to control the ball and back a clean pass. Then Williams defends well against Saka from an Arsenal attacking transition.

Pretty subdued start from Forest. The crowd’s spirits were raised there by Delap chasing down Konsa who had the deal with the sun his eyes, but the Forest striker pushed him in the back.

Arsenal enjoying all of the possession so far, and most of it has come in Forest’s half. One or two players on Arsenal’s right/Forest’s left struggling with the low evening sun. Havertz did get in behind but his cross into the middle was too strong.

Arsenal get the game under way, and play short from kick-off.

There will be a degree of pressure on birthday boy James McAtee today to make an impression.

With Morgan Gibbs-White injured, McAtee is likely to take the No 10 position and continue his redemption arc.

McAtee has been revitalised since the arrival of Oliver Glasner and this is a big afternoon for the former England under 21 international.

In honour of nine-year-old Forest fan James Kerry, who died earlier this month of cancer.

We'll wear black armbands this afternoon, as we join our hosts in remembering nine-year-old Nottingham Forest supporter, James Kerry, who passed away earlier this month following a brave battle with cancer. Rest in peace, James ❤️ https://t.co/YFIXnCfJJX

Surely we cannot have another 0-0 in this fixture? Looking at the talent in Arsenal’s front third, and the fact they are playing their two most offensive full-backs, this might be more open than assummed.

Arsenal can cut Manchester City’s lead to three points with a win today but does it all matter?

Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict is threatening to run into next year and this title race feels fake and damaged.

It is a sham of a season with the prospect of asterisks all over the Premier League campaign.

Arsenal can only carry on as normal as they defend their title but this is an unsatisfactory mess.

The margins are really small and it’s a team and a manager that we know really well, extraordinary manager, really well organised.

They are dangerous in many areas, a very well set-up team and you need to be very tight, very neat, very efficient in everything that you do. You have to insist and insist, and then there’s a lot of volume of actions.

[On coming from behind] Yes, and it’s part of the game, your capacity when something doesn’t go as planned to react and still win the game, and we know the challenge that we have here. In the last two years, we haven’t been able to win here and that’s an opportunity as well to show what we are made of.

Another reason Arsenal will be feeling confident today is Forest’s abysmal home form in the Premier League.

It may surprise neutrals outside of Nottingham but results at the City Ground have been poor for some time.

Indeed, it is just two league wins in 11 months in front of their own supporters which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Before this game, Forest’s head coach Oliver Glasner said: “We have to change it. I spoke to one or two experienced lads who know Forest better than I do and talked about the situation. But if you always talk about the problem it makes it bigger and bigger.

“We haven’t scored a goal at home yet or won a game at home, and that is what we have to change.”

Trips to the City Ground have seldom been easy for Mikel Arteta, with two successive 0-0 draws in the Premier League.

An FA Cup defeat in Jan 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparked a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

Yet Arsenal have secured two wins in a row since that defeat at Brighton, without being truly at their fluent best, and will be confident against a Forest team without injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White.

Fascinating stuff from Sam Dean this morning, who has profiled a member of Mikel Arteta’s inner circle who is not listed on Arsenal’s website. Germán Castaños, an expert in innovation who has written multiple books on alternative thinking, has become a key member of the team. Find out more about Arsenal’s mystery man and his methods here.

In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

#1216. Carles Puyol Named His Toughest Opponent Out Of Rooney, Henry & Drogba

Carles Puyol is widely considered one of football's finest defenders, having played a pivotal part in Barcelona and Spain's successful eras throughout the 2000s and 2010s, leading both sides to an impressive collection of major trophies.

A six-time UEFA Team of the Year nominee, Puyol secured six La Liga championships during his career at the Nou Camp, alongside three Champions League crowns, two Spanish Cups and several other domestic and international accolades.

On the international stage, he was a key figure in Spain's defence during their back-to-back tournament successes, helping La Roja claim Euro 2008 and the 2010 World Cup. He featured in every game of the latter competition and netted a crucial semi-final winner against Germany.

Although he previously identified players such as Arjen Robben and Sergio Aguero as some of the toughest rivals of his career, Puyol was recently challenged to select the most difficult opponent from three former Premier League greats: Thierry Henry, Didier Drogba and Wayne Rooney.

Puyol, speaking with former Manchester United centre-back Rio Ferdinand, was asked to identify the toughest challenge between Henry, Drogba and Rooney. He singled out the first two, highlighting Henry's display in the 2006 Champions League final:

“Henry and Drogba. Henry in the final in 2006 was amazing, and Drogba, many times, fighting.”

Henry and Puyol first crossed paths in the 2006 Champions League final, which saw Barcelona come from behind to secure a 2-1 victory thanks to goals from Samuel Eto’o and Juliano Belletti.

The pair also went head-to-head at the 2006 World Cup in Germany, where France eliminated Spain with a 3-1 win in the Round of 16. Franck Ribery, Patrick Vieira and Zinedine Zidane were all on target for Les Bleus.

In 2007, Henry joined Puyol at Barcelona, arriving for a reported transfer fee of £16m after spending eight successful years with Arsenal, where he established himself as the club's record goalscorer with 228 strikes and one of the greatest strikers in football history.

Henry spent the next three seasons alongside Puyol at the Nou Camp, playing an important role in Barcelona's remarkable 2009 campaign. The Catalan side claimed six trophies that year, completing a historic treble as part of an unprecedented sextuple.

The former France international recorded 121 appearances for Barcelona, registering 49 goals and 27 assists, before making the move to New York Red Bulls in July 2010.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Henry and Puyol featured together in 96 Barcelona matches, recording 65 victories.

Puyol also encountered Drogba on nine occasions at club and international level, with five of those clashes taking place across Champions League campaigns during the striker's Chelsea career.

The Barcelona captain won just the opening three encounters against Drogba, while their final meeting came in the 2011/12 Champions League semi-finals, when Chelsea progressed with a 3-2 aggregate triumph.

Chelsea went on to lift the Champions League trophy for the first time in their history that season. Drogba played a decisive role in the final against Bayern Munich, scoring a late equaliser to force extra time before converting the winning penalty in the shootout.

#1215. Be warned, JJ Gabriel: The SEVEN wonderkids who flopped after making high-profile moves - as Man United star, 16, closes in on move to Real Madrid - but there is cause for optimism

Published: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:29 EST, 23 November 2026

In a sport obsessed with the next big thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

The latest player to have fans raving is former Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel, 16, who joined the club aged nine but stunned those at Old Trafford by asking to leave. He is now closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

The acrimonious nature of the teenager's departure has left Gabriel vulnerable to a spectacular fall from grace, particularly after his team released montages showing him joining an agency and saying goodbye to United.

The spotlight is well and truly burning on Gabriel, and he would do well to learn the lessons of other youngsters who were tipped for greatness but ultimately crashed and burned.

Of course, injuries, personal issues and media pressure can all weigh heavily on a young player's prospects. There are countless pitfalls that mean tomorrow's stars often burn out before they have had the chance to shine.

Here, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over some of the most famous wonderkids who never managed to live up to their potential.

Wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 16, confirmed his exit from Manchester United on Tuesday night

In 2004, Freddy Adu was viewed as the future of American football. Dubbed 'The Next Pele', the Ghanaian-born talent was the youngest professional athlete in major American sports when he signed his first contract at just 14.

The hype was extraordinary. He became MLS's highest-paid player, secured a lucrative Nike contract and appeared in an advert alongside Pele himself.

But things never quite worked out for the attacking midfielder. After three years at DC United and Real Salt Lake, he made the much-anticipated move to Europe, joining Benfica for £1million in 2007. It was largely downhill from there.

After making just 11 appearances in three years in Portugal, he moved to Monaco before embarking on a series of unsuccessful and increasingly disappointing loan spells in Portugal, Turkey and Greece. He eventually ended up at Brazilian club Bahia in 2013.

From that point, Adu floated around clubs in Brazil, Serbia, Finland, the US and Sweden. He last played competitive fooball for Swedish third-tier side Osterlen in 2021, aged 32. He remains one of football's biggest 'what if' stories.

Freddy Adu was dubbed 'The Next Pele' but he never fulfilled anywhere near his potential

Once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as 'the best player I have ever seen at his age', Ravel Morrison is a particularly unfortunate case of an English prospect failing to make the most of an extraordinarily promising career.

As a fresh-faced 17-year-old, he arrived at Carrington with the talent and ability to become one of the world's best players.

He had all the attributes of a world-class attacking midfielder and appeared mature beyond his years on the pitch. Off it, however, was a different story.

In early 2011, barely a year after signing his first professional contract with Manchester United, he was charged with witness intimidation in connection with a domestic violence case.

Since then, although he has never served time in prison, Morrison has faced several further charges, including assault, harassment and fraud. His repeated off-field troubles ultimately derailed a career that had once promised so much.

Morrison has gone on to represent 15 clubs during a career spanning 16 years, failing to fulfil the promise that once enchanted Ferguson. He is currently plying his trade in the second tier of UAE football.

Ravel Morrison was one of the most talented players to come through Man United's academy

The first Brazilian on this list is former Manchester City forward Robinho. Having come through the Santos academy – a production line that has also delivered the likes of Pele and Neymar – he was expected to become the next superstar to emerge from the club's illustrious ranks.

However, a series of setbacks meant he never quite fulfilled that early promise. Robinho followed in the footsteps of Brazilian stars such as Adriano, Dani Alves and Kaka by moving to Europe at a young age, joining Real Madrid in 2005.

He enjoyed a promising start to his career, making more than 100 appearances for Los Blancos and winning two league titles before turning 24.

But his move to Manchester City in 2008 failed to take his career to the next level. In fact, things began to unravel.

The Brazilian did not get off to the best of starts. Upon arriving in Manchester, he revealed that 'Chelsea had made a great proposal, and I accepted'.

What followed were two underwhelming years at the Etihad, where he scored 16 goals in 53 appearances and spent much of his second season in England sidelined by injury.

Robinho subsequently joined AC Milan before spells with a number of Turkish clubs and a return to Brazil. He never again reached the heights of his early career.

The Brazilian is currently imprisoned after being found guilty of sexual assault in connection with an incident at a Milan nightclub in 2013. He began serving his nine-year sentence in 2024.

Former Man City star Robinho never quite fulfilled the early promise he had back in Brazil

Another case reminiscent of Adu's: a young superstar who was seemingly rated too highly before we ever really got to see him play.

Mastour caught the eye of Italian giants AC Milan after gaining notoriety on YouTube. His video, uploaded in 2012 and titled 'The Best 14-year-old in the World', showcased the Moroccan's impressive array of skills and tricks, making him one of football's first viral sensations.

The hype surrounding Mastour was staggering, with the youngster securing a lucrative endorsement deal with Nike. Before long, he was posing alongside Neymar in a photoshoot.

But the success never materialised for the tricky forward. During four years on AC Milan's books, he failed to make a single first-team appearance and managed just six outings during loan spells at Malaga and Dutch side PEC Zwolle.

The Moroccan, now 28, plays in the fourth tier of Italian football. Quite how such a highly rated prospect failed to fulfil his potential remains a mystery.

Hachim Mastour dazzled as a teenager on the internet but ended up a long way from the top

From one player who never showed his quality to one who only a decade ago was the recipient of the coveted Golden Boy award for the best under-21 player in Europe.

Renato Sanches was an absolute phenomenon, the box-to-box midfielder burst onto the scene in the 2015-16 season at Benfica – earning himself a place on the plane to France with Portugal for the 2016 Euros where he played a pivotal role in his nation's triumph.

Those performances saw a host of European giants fight it out to land the then-18-year-old, with Bayern Munich emerging triumphant – landing the midfielder in a deal rising to £63million.

However, Sanches failed to hit his stride in Germany and he was soon shipped out on loan to Swansea – where he was best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

He enjoyed a small resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, paving the way for a move to PSG. But once again, the big transfer failed to work out, and he now finds himself with Greek side Panathinaikos.

However, Sanches struggled to find his feet in Germany and was soon sent out on loan to Swansea, where he is perhaps best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

He enjoyed a resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, which paved the way for a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

But once again, a big-money move failed to work out, and he now finds himself at Greek side Panathinaikos.

Renato Sanches (pictured at Roma in 2024) now plies his trade in Greece with Panathinaikos

Alexandre Pato had the world at his feet, but his body ultimately failed to deliver on the extraordinary talent he possessed.

The Brazilian was an electric centre-forward who lit up European football. His goal against Barcelona in the Champions League, scored after just 24 seconds at the age of 22, was a perfect illustration of his frightening ability.

His pace, agility and clinical finishing saw him touted as a future world-beater, while he was named Golden Boy.

Alexandre Pato is another wonderkid who saw their career hampered by a string of injuries

Yet persistent injury problems made it almost impossible for Pato to fulfil his early promise.

The Brazilian struggled with ankle, Achilles and muscle problems throughout his career. As the injuries mounted, his outstanding physical attributes began to wane, rendering the qualities that had once terrified defenders increasingly ineffective.

After six years at AC Milan, Pato returned to Brazil to join Corinthians. He spent two years with the club before embarking on short spells at Chelsea and Villarreal, neither of which yielded lasting success.

Rounding off this list is another English talent who once looked destined for the very top but has since seen his career take a downward turn.

Back in 2019, there were few hotter prospects in world football than Jadon Sancho. The then 19-year-old had made the brave decision two years earlier to leave England, having spent several impressive years in Manchester City's academy, and join Bundesliga giants Borussia Dortmund.

It seemed a bizarre move at the time, but the switch proved to be a stroke of genius. Sancho was handed regular first-team football and flourished, registering 40 goals and 54 assists in just 118 Bundesliga appearances. He also collected a DFB-Pokal winner's medal.

By 2021, the boy from Kennington had the world at his feet, with a host of suitors willing to break the bank to secure his services.

Jadon Sancho once had the world at his feet but has found himself stuck in a downward spiral

After a summer-long transfer saga, Sancho eventually joined Manchester United for an eye-watering £73million, reportedly earning £350,000 per week. It proved to be a nightmare move for both parties.

The Englishman had to wait until late November to score his first United goal in his debut season and never consistently rediscovered his best form.

In January 2024, he returned to Germany and enjoyed a revival, helping guide Dortmund to the Champions League final, where they lost to Real Madrid at Wembley.

Two unsuccessful loan spells at Chelsea and Aston Villa followed before Sancho left United as a free agent last summer. He remains without a club at the age of 26, just five years after his mega-money move.

For all the promising youngsters who struggle to live up to the hype, there are also teen sensations who navigate the pitfalls of professional football to achieve great things.

Kylian Mbappe helped Monaco win their first Ligue 1 title for 17 years having broken into the team as a 16-year-old. His progress since then has been remarkable and he remains one of the world's very best at Real Madrid.

His team-mate Vinicius Jr signed for Real Madrid to much fanfare as an 18-year-old and has lived up to it all for both club and country.

While you could argue that Neymar could have achieved more, he has still enjoyed a stellar career across the globe and become the highest-scoring Brazilian player in history for the national side after signing for Barcelona, as one of the most talked-about starlets.

Wayne Rooney broke through for Everton at 16 and went on to have a brilliant career

When you look closer to home, Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as exciting 16-year-olds and both reached the very highest level.

Paolo Maldini made his AC Milan debut at 16 and became one of the all-time great centre-backs and Cesc Fabregas developed into a world class midfielder after getting selected at the same age for Arsenal.

Going back further, Diego Maradona was playing senior football at 15, as did Ronaldo Nazario, while Lionel Messi embarked on his extraordinary career at 16.

JJ Gabriel and his management will be hoping that when all is said and done - his name is associated with this category and avoid joining the starlets who never quite made it.

#1214. Alajbegovic half-time withdrawal not a major concern for Juventus

Kerim Alajbegovic underwent medical examinations in Turin on Monday after coming off at half-time during Juventus’s 4-0 victory over Venezia on Sunday evening, and the initial reports indicate that there is no major injury concern for the young Bosnian talent.

The 19-year-old was replaced by goalscorer Nick Woltemade at half-time of Juventus’s 4-0 win over Venezia on Sunday, their first game back since the November international break; Alajbegovic playing the full 90 minutes in both of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Nations League matches.

The youngster reported for tests at JMedical on Monday afternoon, and according to reports from Gianluca Di Marzio and various others, he is suffering from a slight muscular overload in his right leg.

His condition is set to be monitored day by day, but he is not expected to be ruled out for a significant period of time.

Gianluca Di Marzio suggests that Luciano Spalletti could even have Alajbegovic back in time for Juventus’s upcoming Europa League fixture against Omonoia at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday evening, although he could be minded to give the youngster a rest.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1213. Gerrard Slams Pochettino's 'Disrespectful' Treatment of Man Utd Star

Things couldn't have gone much worse for Mauricio Pochettino in his first outing as Manchester United manager. He watched on as his new side were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield.

The Argentine's pre-game plans quickly went out the window when Lenny Yoro picked up a red card inside the first 10 minutes. He was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as the last defender, and Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick.

Down to 10 men, the away team buckled completely, with Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz scoring to deliver all three points for Liverpool. Pochettino's 4-0 loss is the joint-worst debut result any Man Utd manager has suffered in club history.

Clearly, Pochettino has a lot of work to do if he is to improve Man Utd. Beyond the result, he's perhaps already made an early misstep with his treatment of one senior star. Steven Gerrard certainly thinks so.

Speaking on The Overlap, Gerrard claimed that the decision to drop Harry Maguire in favour of Matthijs de Ligt was wrong. He began:

"I thought he got it wrong. I thought he got it wrong in the back line. I think to start someone in a game of that magnitude, it's the biggest game in the country. All eyes are on it all over the world."

Gerrard then claimed Pochettino's call showed a lack of respect for Maguire:

"Forget the youngsters that are maybe not ready at the moment. Matthijs de Ligt's been out for a year. Harry Maguire's their best defender at the moment. He should have started the game.

"He's one who is rolling his sleeves up and having a go. Okay, he hasn't been perfect, but to not play him and put De Ligt in before him, I thought it was a bit disrespectful."

Due to the red card, Maguire came on in the first half and Gerrard praised the Englishman's efforts, suggesting they were enough to prove he should have started: "And he made a difference when he came on. And he was one who was putting his body on the line.

"He made a great block, I think it was around the 38th, 39th minute, which stopped a certain goal. And I've watched Manchester United a lot this season, and he's one who's having a go."

It's not looking good for the Red Devils.

Pochettino may well have his eye on the January transfer market as a way to improve his struggling squad. After all, defenders Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw will all enter the final six months of their contracts this winter.

However, Gerrard has questioned the club's chances of landing an upgrade in the short term. He explained: "Who's going to let world-class centre-halves go in January? Unless someone's prepared to pay astronomical money. That's what's going to have to happen."

As such, Pochettino may well have to make do for the rest of the season with what he has available to him already. If that's the case, he'd best hope Maguire didn't find his treatment as 'disrespectful' as Gerrard suggests.

#1212. Matthijs de Ligt is Fast Becoming Man Utd's New Paul Pogba

Mauricio Pochettino faces an uphill battle to reverse Manchester United's fortunes this season, and improving some of his players' performances seems like a lost cause at the moment.

The Red Devils were thumped 4-0 by rivals Liverpool at Anfield in their first game under their new boss. Leny Yoro's early red card put the away side in a perilous position, and goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz ultimately punished them.

The result leaves United in the Premier League's bottom three, just a single point above rock-bottom Crystal Palace. Things look precarious for the north-west side, and they desperately need some of their senior players to stand up in this period of adversity.

It's up to Pochettino to elicit performances from these more experienced stars, although the players themselves need to take some accountability.

Bruno Fernandes' petulance and misguided leadership techniques are derailing United, while Lisandro Martinez's recent outburst against the club's hierarchy shows he's not the man Pochettino can turn to.

Diogo Dalot is in horrendous form, Youri Tielemans' declining physical attributes are putting him in trouble, and Harry Maguire is at the eleventh hour of his career.

This leaves Matthijs de Ligt as one of the remaining senior players Pochettino might hope will step forward and lead this dysfunctional dressing room, but there are unfortunately huge question marks around the £195,000-a-week Dutchman as well.

When United signed De Ligt for around £43 million back in the summer of 2024, there was still considerable hope that he could live up to the potential he displayed in his early days at Ajax.

The Netherlands international was viewed as Europe's best centre-back prodigy when he broke through in Amsterdam, so much so that he won the Kopa Trophy in 2019. A respectable but uninspiring three-year stint at Juventus was followed by a slightly underwhelming spell at Bayern Munich.

United offered him the chance to revitalise his career two years ago, after it'd become clear that he had no future at the Allianz Arena. A promising debut season at Old Trafford suggested that there was still life in him, but a turbulent last 12 months have raised serious question marks.

Between November 30th 2025 and October 21st 2026, De Ligt didn't play a minute of football due to a back injury. He's returned to the fold over the last month, but only managed his first Premier League minutes back on Sunday at Anfield, and his dire performance was a reminder of why his career has stalled over the last three or four years.

The 27-year-old struggled to deal with the intensity of Liverpool's press, being caught out in possession multiple times, while his positional play defensively was all at sea.

While this was certainly a difficult environment for him to come back into, and Pochettino's decision to throw the defender into this game was questionable, it's still difficult to envisage a world where De Ligt re-establishes himself as a dependable option in this United squad.

In many ways, there are comparisons to be made between the former Ajax man and Paul Pogba. The Frenchman was deemed one of Europe's most promising young talents at some point, had a spell at Juventus and then was largely disappointing after making the switch to United.

Like De Ligt, Pogba was hindered by injury issues, although it's undeniable that neither player displayed the consistency their elite talent as a youngster suggested they should've.

The midfielder was scrutinised far more than his defensive counterpart, partly because United forked out significantly more money to bring him to Manchester. However, Pogba arguably delivered much more for the Red Devils than De Ligt has at any point, contributing to a couple of relatively encouraging seasons where the north-west outfit secured top-two finishes.

The Argentine quickly learned the mess he's tasked with cleaning up.

Ultimately, however, the parallels are there. Teenage sensations who moved to United to fulfil their potential, but failed to do so, with injuries playing their part in their failure.

De Ligt can still resurrect his career at Old Trafford, but it looks increasingly unlikely. It wouldn't be a surprise to see him plying his trade at a club of Monaco's stature when he enters his early 30s, just like Pogba.
